courses.profile: Large, flat galloping Mildmay course plus the unique Grand National course
courses.pace: Handy, fluent jumpers are favoured; National fences demand rhythm and bravery
courses.drawHeadline: N/A – no stalls over jumps
courses.angle: Upgrade economical jumpers with Aintree or similar flat-track form
courses.trap: Do not treat Mildmay and Grand National courses as the same test
courses.groundNote: National course can ride much more exacting than its flat topography suggests.

going.firm: Firm is uncommon. On quick ground, efficient jumping and tactical speed are valuable without a strong universal pace bias.
going.good: Generally fair. Efficient jumping, rhythm and race shape matter more than one fixed run style.
going.soft: A stronger stamina test; mistakes become more costly. Horses can still come from off the pace if they travel.
going.heavy: Deep-ground stamina and jumping under fatigue dominate. Be wary of doubtful stayers and fragile jumpers.

courses.profile: Galloping; stiff uphill finish; straight course to 1m and round course

courses.drawHeadline: Recent straight-course data leans high at 5–8f; highly meeting- and ground-dependent
courses.angle: On straight course, map pace by side before judging the stall
courses.trap: Assuming a permanent high/low bias without watching earlier races
courses.groundNote: Soft ground and the uphill finish can make every distance ride longer.

going.firm: Fast early but still demanding late. Leaders must ration speed; jumpers need to stay efficient.
going.good: A fair but stamina-aware test under both codes. Save enough for the finish.
going.soft: Becomes strongly stamina-led, especially over jumps. Upgrade proven soft-ground stayers.
going.heavy: Can be gruelling. Deep-ground stamina and jumping under pressure dominate tactical speed.

draw.reading: Moderate only; straight-course pace/ground can override.
